text:
samir: Hey team — after the Acme org merge a subset of our users (including me) suddenly can't open the Phoenix project in the console. We get a 403 'permission denied'. Happens for multiple accounts in the same AD group.

emily: Sorry you're hitting this, @samir. Can you paste the exact repro steps and one example user email?

samir: steps:
1) sign in via Okta
2) click org dropdown -> select Phoenix project
3) console shows blank project page with a modal: "403 Permission Denied"
user: samir@acme.com (we're on SAML SCIM group sync)
Screenshot: https://imgur.com/a/example (shared by the customer)

emily: Thanks. Can you also run this quick API check from an affected user to confirm it's not just UI?
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.com/v1/projects/phoenix"
```
Expected: 200. Actual: 403 with body `{"error":{"code":403,"message":"forbidden"}}`

kevin: @emily — SCIM sync for Acme completed yesterday morning. I pulled the SCIM diff and group membership looks intact. However I see a couple of users flagged with a 'pending_remap' event in our import logs.

lara: can you paste the trace id from the 403 response (console devtools or API X-Request-Id)? That helps check routing for project role evaluation.

samir: X-Request-Id: req_0a7f3b2c

emily: copied. @maria @lara I dug into the audit: there are two events right around the merge time where role inheritance was recalculated for org -> projects and a script toggled an experimental flag 'preserve-legacy-inherit=false'. Could be related. Maria any idea?

maria: I see that flag flip in the deploy log. It was part of a small rollout to tighten inherited role resolution. We rolled back the flag 2h later but some users were evaluated in-between. Sounds like a race where group membership changes + the flag change produced stale bindings.

emily: Ok, immediate mitigation for the customer: can you try forcing a membership resync from our admin CLI as a workspace admin? This will re-evaluate inherited roles for Phoenix.

kevin: here's the admin command (run from our ops workstation):
```bash
redwood org members resync --org=acme --project=phoenix --force
```
Note: this is safe but may take a few minutes depending on member count.

samir: ran the resync as instructed; still seeing 403 for two users, one user regained access.

emily: ok thanks — we need an additional step: for stuck users, temporarily reassign a direct project role then remove it after a clean resync. Example (ops UI or CLI):
```bash
redwood projects grant-role --project=phoenix --user=stuck.user@acme.com --role=viewer
redwood projects revoke-role --project=phoenix --user=stuck.user@acme.com --role=viewer
```

lara: filing an internal investigation — tagging eng-sre and eng-platform. @incidents-bot creating ticket and runbook. :eyes:

incidents-bot: Created support ticket #4352 and assigned to eng-sre (priority: P2). Attached logs: scim-import-2954443000.log, role-eval-req_0a7f3b2c.log

emily: Thanks — I've shared the temporary workaround with the customer (resync + direct grant/revoke). We're escalating to eng for a fix to ensure role inheritance recalcs are idempotent across flag flips.

maria: I'll add a regression test to catch this sequence (SCIM group change + flag toggle) and schedule a hotfix if we can reproduce reliably.

samir: Appreciate the quick help. Please keep me posted in this thread and confirm once all affected accounts are back. :thumbsup:

emily: Will do — assigning owner: @maria (eng-platform) and follow-ups to @lara (sre) and @kevin (idp).
